source.name: Inspiration4 clinical blood panels (NASA Open Science Data Repository)
source.mission: Inspiration4 (SpaceX, September 2021): 4 civilian crew, about 3 days in orbit
source.citation: Please cite NASA OSDR studies OSD-569 and OSD-575 and the Inspiration4 / SOMA publications.

analytes.name: HEMATOCRIT
analytes.label: Hematocrit (% of blood that is red cells)

method.plain_text: Each person's normal = the average of their 3 pre-flight tests. A later value is flagged when it is more than 2 'typical spreads' away from that normal (|z| > 2).

shared_finding.label: MCV (average red blood cell size)

sensitivity.plain_text: With a stricter rule (minimum spread 10% of the lab range instead of 5%), 1 of 4 would be flagged. So the flag count depends on that choice; the direction (lower than every pre-flight test in 4 of 4) does not.

shared_finding.plain_text: One day after landing, MCV (average red blood cell size) was lower than usual in 4 of 4 crew members (on average 4.0% lower than their own pre-flight average). In 4 of 4 it was lower than every one of their own pre-flight tests. 4 of 4 values were still inside the normal lab range, so a standard one-size-fits-all check would not have noticed it; comparing each person with their own normal does.

noise_control.chance_note: Rough estimate: if every flag were noise at the pre-flight rate (26.2%) and analytes were independent, about 0.17 of 37 analytes would be flagged in all 4 people by chance.
noise_control.plain_text: Sanity check without any spaceflight: we scored the last pre-flight test (L-3) against the two earlier ones (L-92, L-44). 26.2% of tests were flagged there, vs 20.4% one day after landing. So a single flag on its own is mostly normal day-to-day noise. The signal worth trusting is the same change showing up in every crew member.

limitations.title: Only 4 people
limitations.text: With n=4, nothing here is statistically proven. It shows the method working on real data, not a medical conclusion.

limitations.title: Only 3 'normal' tests per person
limitations.text: Each person's normal comes from 3 pre-flight blood tests. That is too few to know their natural spread well, so we use a minimum spread (5% of the lab range width); it was needed for 28 of 147 person-analyte series.

limitations.title: A 3-day mission, not a Mars trip
limitations.text: Inspiration4 lasted about 3 days. A Mars mission takes years, so these data cannot tell us what happens on long flights.

limitations.title: Single flags are often noise
limitations.text: 26.2% of tests were flagged even before flight, vs 20.4% after. Only changes seen in the whole crew are worth attention.

limitations.title: Not medical advice
limitations.text: A flag means 'different from this person's usual', not 'sick'. Day R+1 is also affected by re-entry, travel and fluid shifts, not only by time in orbit.
